tagline: Down the Delaware to the cliffs of the Hawk's Nest.
intro: Out of Hancock, NY 97 follows the Delaware River about 70 miles down to Port Jervis, with Pennsylvania across the water, through rolling hills and a string of river hamlets, Callicoon, Narrowsburg, Barryville and Pond Eddy among them. For long stretches the railroad keeps it company.
The road was a long time coming. The legislature laid out a route along the river in 1911, when much of it existed in name only, and the whole highway did not open until August 30, 1939.

moments.title: Callicoon
moments.text: Dutch hunters named the place Kollikoonkill, Wild Turkey Creek, for the birds they found here, and when the Erie Railroad came through it became Callicoon Depot.

moments.title: Roebling's Delaware Aqueduct
moments.text: At Minisink Ford the oldest wire suspension bridge left in the country opened in 1849 to carry canal boats over the river, and after the canal closed it was drained for wagons.

moments.title: Hawk's Nest
moments.text: A few miles north of Port Jervis the road winds tight along the face of the cliffs above the Delaware.
